Final Project Instructions

Project 1: Data Modeling & CRUD System
Design a data model, then build a working PHP
-
Based CRUD application
50%
Design a Complete Data Model
Cover all three levels: Conceptual (entities & relationships), Logical (attributes & keys), and
Physical (tables, data types, constraints).
Implement as a Functional Web System
Build a working PHP application that supports all four basic CRUD operations: Create, Read,
Update, and Delete.
Choose a PHP Coding Approach
Object
-
Oriented (OOP), PDO, or Procedural (Preferred). Procedural PHP is recommended for this course level, but other approaches are also accepted. Prepare Documentation Include your ER diagram and a brief explanation of design decisions showing the relationship between your data model and the system.
Project 2: Open
Source PHP Project Customization
Find, study, customize, and present an existing PHP project
Find a Suitable PHP Project
Source from any reputable free repository. Suggested site: www.sourcecodester.com/php

 any other available open
-
Source PHP repository.
Study the Project Thoroughly
Understand its code structure, database design, and how each module works before presenting it.
Customize or Enhance the Project
Add UI improvements, a new feature or module, or adapt the system to a new use case. The group must demonstrate understanding, not just run the original source.
Cite the Original Source
Include the project title, author (if available), and URL clearly in your documentation and during your presentation.
General Requirements (Both Projects)
Rules that apply to both projects " Each group must have exactly 3 members. Both projects are submitted and presented by the same team. " Presentation may be done online or face
-
Face on the instructor
Assigned date. Each group must be ready to demo both projects live. " Projects must run on a local server environment (e.g., XAMPP, WAMP, or Laragon) using a MySQL or MariaDB database. " Submit all project files, database SQL files, and complete group documentation on or before the presentation date. " All members must be able to explain and answer questions about both projects. Individual understanding will be part of the evaluation.

This guide explains the expected contents, format, and structure of each section of your group documentation.

1.3 Data Model
Required diagrams and descriptions " Conceptual Model  Entity
-
Relationship Diagram (ERD) showing all entities and their relationships. Label cardinality (one
Many, many
Many, etc.). " Logical Model  Refined ERD with all attributes, primary keys (PK), and foreign keys (FK) identified. " Physical Model 
Actual database schema showing table names, column names, data types
(INT, VARCHAR, DATE, etc.), constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT), and indexes. " Brief narrative  
2 paragraphs explaining your design decisions (why you chose those
Entities, how relationships are structured).
1.4 CRUD Functionality Description
For each module in your system, describe the four CRUD operations. Use the table format below as a guide:
Module / Table
Create Read Update Delete e.g., Students Add new student View student list Edit student info Remove student (add more rows)
1.5 Screenshots
Include at least one screenshot per CRUD operation (minimum 4 screenshots). Label each screenshot
Clearly, e.g., "Figure 1: Add New Student Form."
1.6 Database SQL File
Attach or embed your exported SQL file (.sql). It must include both the CREATE TABLE statements and sample INSERT data so the evaluator can restore and test the system.

4.3 Grading Rubric
 Project 1 (Data Modeling & CRUD)
Data Model Quality (Conceptual,
Logical, Physical) All three models are complete, accurate, and clearly labeled. Relationships and keys are correct. Two out of three models are present with minor errors. Only one model present or major errors in design. CRUD Functionality All four operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) work correctly without errors. Three operations work; minor bugs present. Two or fewer operations work or system fails to run. Code Quality Code is clean, well
-
Structured, and follows the chosen approach
(OOP / PDO /
Procedural) consistently. Code works but lacks structure or consistency. Code is disorganized, hard to follow, or copied without understanding. Documentation All required sections are complete, clear, and professionally presented. Most sections present; some are incomplete or vague. Documentation is missing major sections. Presentation & Q&A All members present confidently. Questions answered correctly and clearly. Presentation is adequate; some questions partially answered. Members unable to explain their own work or answer basic questions.
